_comment: The corpus of RFC 0030, section 17.5, read by scripts/corpus-gate.py; test/corpus/README.md
documents every field. Each project is pinned to a 40-hex `sha` and checked out once into
<workdir>/<project>. Each config names the files it analyses (`compile`: per-file
weavec-cc -c, and weavec --whole-program over all of them when `wholeProgram` is true;
--legacy runs the v0.10.0 weavec tool exactly as scripts/corpus.py did). `build`, `test`
and `bench` commands run under /bin/sh in a fresh copy of the checkout with CC set to the
compiler (a wrapper around weavec-cc, or the reference compiler), JOBS to the parallelism,
SUPPORT to test/corpus/support/<project> and BENCH to test/corpus/bench. `{support}` in
compile arguments expands to the same support directory. `lowered` holds the only allowed
-Wno-error=weavec-<id> flags, each next to the fingerprint of its triaged-true definite
error. `gates` carries the limits of gates G9-G15, and `gates.heldOut` those of RFC 0031's
G5, G6 and G12 for the configs marked `heldOut` (RFC 0031, section 11.2: the eleven held-out
projects, run by --full and by --held-out). RFC 0033, section 11: a config marked heldOut may
name a `set`, `fresh` (its eight projects, run by --full and by --held-out, gated by D1 and D5
under `gates.rfc0033`) or `sealed` (five projects, run only by --sealed or --only, built with
the reference compiler alone until gate D2). RFC 0034, section 9: two more sets, `fresh34`
(ten projects, run by --full, --held-out and --set fresh34, gated by F1, F5 and F7 under
`gates.rfc0034`; the only held-out configs with a `bench`) and `sealed34` (five projects, run
only by --set sealed34 or --only, built with the reference compiler alone until gate F2).

mustReport.note: minigzip's repeated fclose(stdout): gz_uncompress closes stdout on every iteration of the -c -d loop (v0.10.0: error, double-free)

G14._comment: RFC 0032 R6 as amended (Implementation amendments, 3): user CPU of the default build (with the runtime), of the build with -fno-weavec-runtime, and the default build's peak resident size, each over the reference compiler's.

rfc0032._comment: RFC 0032 R4: the unresolved share of each facet over the original configs together and over the held-out configs together.

heldOut._comment: RFC 0031's gates over the configs marked heldOut (section 11.2), which G9 and G10 do not count: G5 (no definite error triaged false; with --full every build and test suite passes with no trap), G6 (their unresolved temporal share together, program ledgers where a whole-program analysis exists and unit ledgers otherwise) and G12 (the single-unit compiles of mujs one.c and sqlite3.c; the weavec-cc build's CPU time against the reference compiler's is reported, not limited). G6's limit is the ratchet of RFC 0031's *Gates carried forward*. G15's over-budget share counts them with the original configs (RFC 0031 G11).

rfc0033._comment: RFC 0033's gates over the configs of set fresh (section 11), which G9, G10, G11 and RFC 0031's held-out gates do not count: D1 (no definite error triaged false; with --full every build and test suite passes, in trap mode with no trap and in report mode with no failure) and D5 (with --full the weavec-cc build's CPU time over the reference compiler's, per config). The sealed configs get the same values under rfc0033.sealed.*, from the one --sealed run of gate D2.

rfc0034._comment: RFC 0034's gates (Acceptance gates). F1 over the configs of set fresh34 (section 9): every build passes with the default flags (or stops only at definite errors triaged true) and every test suite passes, in trap mode with no trap and in report mode with no failure. F2: the same over set sealed34, with F5's build ratio, from the one --set sealed34 run. F5: with --full each config's weavec-cc build CPU time at most maxBuildRatio times the reference compiler's (every config but sealed34 ones; the reference compiler builds each once more); the single-unit compiles of maxUnitCpuSeconds within their CPU seconds; no compilation above maxCompileRssMiB (the per-file compiles of --quick, and every compiler process of a --full trap-mode build). F7: with --bench the default build's run time (with the runtime) over the reference compiler's: each fresh34 workload at most maxOverhead and their geometric mean at most maxGeometricMean; RFC 0032's G14 benchmarks at maxOverheadG14.

configs.name: sds
configs.notes: Simple dynamic strings: realloc-heavy, returns owned pointers with a header offset. The test is the library's own sds-test (SDS_TEST_MAIN).

configs.name: cJSON
configs.notes: Tree of malloc'd nodes freed recursively; custom allocator hooks via function pointers. The build is the project's CMake build with the unity tests and cJSON_Utils; ENABLE_CUSTOM_COMPILER_FLAGS=Off drops its -Werror, which would promote any compiler's new warnings.

configs.name: cJSON-program
configs.notes: cJSON_Utils.c calls into cJSON.c (cJSON_free, cJSON_Delete, cJSON_Duplicate, ...); analysed as one program. Built and tested with the cJSON config.

configs.name: jsmn
configs.notes: Header-only parser; the examples are the translation units. The tests are the project's four test/tests.c builds (make test compiles and runs them).

configs.name: log.c
configs.notes: Callbacks stored in a global table; FILE* borrowed across calls. No build system and no tests: the per-file compile is the build.

configs.name: printf
configs.notes: Pointer arithmetic over caller buffers with no allocation: a false-positive canary. Its test suite is C++ (test/test_suite.cpp includes printf.c into a C++ unit), outside WeaveC, so the per-file compile is the build.

configs.name: linenoise
configs.notes: History as a global array of strdup'd strings; strdup/free through helpers.

configs.name: linenoise-program
configs.notes: example.c installs the completion and hints callbacks linenoise.c calls through pointers, and frees what linenoise() returns. The build is the project's Makefile (linenoise-example); the test is its pseudo-terminal harness linenoise-test, which drives linenoise-example (102 checks, about 20 s).

configs.name: zlib
configs.notes: Allocation through zalloc/zfree function pointers stored in the stream; windows and tables freed in deflateEnd/inflateEnd; gz* wraps FILE-like state. The build is zlib's own ./configure && make -j8 (static and shared example and minigzip); the test is make test.

configs.name: lua
configs.notes: A garbage-collected VM. realloc through the l_alloc function pointer, a 968-block interpreter loop with computed goto (luaV_execute), linked stacks of locals in the parser. The build is the developer makefile with POSIX and dlopen (as LUA_USE_LINUX, which also suits macOS) and without the Linux-only -Wl,-E; the test is the named testes subset below, run by support/lua/subset.lua in user mode. Left out: files.lua (needs /dev/full, missing on macOS), main.lua (stand-alone interpreter tests, skipped in user mode anyway), big.lua and heavy.lua (long), and the T-library tests (need a build with ltests.h).
test: cd testes && ../lua "$SUPPORT/subset.lua" gc.lua db.lua calls.lua strings.lua literals.lua tpack.lua attrib.lua gengc.lua locals.lua constructs.lua code.lua cstack.lua nextvar.lua pm.lua utf8.lua api.lua memerr.lua events.lua vararg.lua closure.lua coroutine.lua goto.lua errors.lua math.lua sort.lua bitwise.lua verybig.lua

configs.name: jansson
configs.notes: A reference-counted JSON library: json_incref/json_decref keep json_t::refcount with __atomic_add_fetch/__atomic_sub_fetch (inline in jansson.h), json_decref frees through json_delete in value.c, containers take a share of what is stored in them. The per-file compiles use the configured headers in support/jansson; the build is the project's CMake build, which configures its own; the test is its CTest suite (API tests and the valid/invalid/encoding suites through json_process).

configs.name: bzip2
configs.notes: Block-sorting compressor. BZ2_bzDecompressInit links a heap DState and the caller's (often stack) bz_stream both ways (s->strm = strm; strm->state = s) and BZ2_bzDecompressEnd frees the state through the stream's allocator hooks (bzalloc/bzfree function pointers). The pinned checkout has CMake and Meson builds only; the build is support/bzip2/bzip2.mk, which mimics the classic Makefile (libbz2.a, bzip2 linked against it and against the objects directly, bzip2recover), and the test is its six-sample round trip for both bzip2 binaries. The per-file compiles use support/bzip2/bz_version.h, which the build generates.

configs.name: hiredis
configs.notes: Redis client: replies are trees freed through a function-pointer table (redisReplyObjectFunctions), commands are formatted into malloc'd strings through out-parameters (redisFormatCommand(&cmd, ...)). The build is the project's Makefile (static library and hiredis-test, without SSL, -Werror as shipped); the test is test.sh, which starts a redis-server on a free port and runs hiredis-test against it (it needs redis-server on PATH), through support/hiredis/run-tests.sh, which tolerates only the two connection-error tests that fail on Darwin with any compiler.

configs.name: http-parser
configs.notes: A callback-driven HTTP parser over caller buffers; the tests keep global pointers to the current message and settings (current_pause_parser points to a local of parse_pause). The build is the project's Makefile (test_g: strict, -O0; test_fast: -O3; bench), -Werror as shipped; the test runs test_g and test_fast (bench is built, not run: about 25 s of throughput measurement).

configs.name: inih
configs.notes: INI parser: a line buffer on the stack or the heap (INI_USE_STACK, INI_ALLOW_REALLOC), callbacks per name/value pair. The build compiles ini.c; the test is tests/unittest.sh, which builds and runs 15 configurations of the unit tests and writes their output over the tracked baselines, which must then be unchanged.
test: cd tests && CC="$CC" bash ./unittest.sh && git diff --exit-code -- .

configs.name: libyaml
configs.notes: YAML parser and emitter: growable buffers described by start/pointer/end triples that yaml_string_extend, yaml_stack_extend and yaml_queue_extend rebase after realloc through out-parameters; a token queue and event and document trees. The build is the project's CMake build with its tests; the test is CTest (version, reader, nesting) and the run-scanner, run-parser, run-loader, run-emitter and run-dumper programs over examples/*.yaml, each of which must report SUCCESS or PASSED for the file (run-parser, given no option, also parses its own argv[0] and reports that as a failure). The per-file compiles use support/libyaml/config.h, which CMake generates.
test: for f in examples/*.yaml; do for t in run-scanner run-parser run-loader run-emitter run-dumper; do out/$t "$f" > "out/$t.log" || exit 1; cat "out/$t.log"; grep -F "'$f'" "out/$t.log" | grep -Eq 'SUCCESS|PASSED' || exit 1; done; done

configs.name: lz4
configs.notes: LZ4 compression: hot copy loops over caller buffers (LZ4_memcpy_using_offset copies within one stack buffer, LZ4_wildCopy8 past the end of the match), frame and HC contexts with custom allocators. The build is the library and the lz4 CLI (lib-release, lz4-release) and the test programs; the test is tests/Makefile's check (the essential CLI tests) and 500 tests each of fuzzer and frametest with seed 1, and decompress-partial. The seed and the number of tests of both are fixed (-s1 -i500): left alone the fuzzer derives its seed from the time, and some seeds (124, at test 299) send LZ4_decompress_safe corrupt input with a match offset of 0, for which LZ4_memcpy_using_offset_base (lib/lz4.c:498) calls memcpy(dstPtr, srcPtr, 2) with srcPtr == dstPtr. The source expects it (`assert(offset != 1)`, and the comment `offset==0 happens on testing` two lines above); memcpy's operands may not overlap, so RFC 0030's `disjoint` check traps there. It is a true finding, independent of the runtime, and a run that reaches it stops the fuzzer.
build: make -j"$JOBS" -C tests CC="$CC" lz4 datagen fuzzer frametest fullbench decompress-partial
test: make -C tests CC="$CC" check test-fuzzer test-frametest test-decompress-partial FUZZER_TIME='-s1 -i500'

configs.name: miniz
configs.notes: Deflate/inflate and ZIP archives: compressor state machines over caller buffers, archive readers and writers with pluggable read/write/alloc callbacks (mz_zip_file_write_func writes a NULL buffer of 0 bytes for an empty entry). The build is the project's CMake build with the examples; the test runs example1, example2 and example6, and round-trips miniz_zip.c through example5 (tdefl/tinfl streaming) and example3 (the buffer API). The per-file compiles use support/miniz/miniz_export.h, which CMake generates.
test: ./bin/example5 c miniz_zip.c out/gate.c5 && ./bin/example5 d out/gate.c5 out/gate.out5 && cmp out/gate.out5 miniz_zip.c
./bin/example3 c miniz_zip.c out/gate.c3 && ./bin/example3 d out/gate.c3 out/gate.out3 && cmp out/gate.out3 miniz_zip.c

configs.name: mujs
configs.notes: A JavaScript interpreter with a mark-and-sweep GC, a bytecode compiler and a backtracking regexp engine. Compile-and-time only (RFC 0031, section 11.2, gate G12): the per-file compile is the single-unit one.c, which includes every source file, and the build is the project's release interpreter and pretty-printer; the test262 suite is not run by the gate.

configs.name: sqlite
configs.notes: The SQLite amalgamation (sqlite3.c, about 260,000 lines in one unit) and its shell. Compile-and-time only (RFC 0031, section 11.2, gate G12): single-threaded, no extension loading; the build compiles both units and links the shell; no test suite is run.

configs.name: tinyexpr
configs.notes: An expression parser and evaluator: te_expr trees with an anonymous union of value, bound variable and function, parameters in a trailing array, freed recursively. The build is the project's Makefile (smoke and smoke_pr run themselves as they are built, the examples and repl); the test reruns the smoke tests and the examples and evaluates one expression in repl (bench is left out: about 10 s).
build: make -j"$JOBS" CC="$CC" smoke smoke_pr example example2 example3 repl

configs.name: utf8proc
configs.notes: Unicode normalization, case mapping and grapheme segmentation over caller buffers, with large generated property tables (utf8proc_data.c, included into utf8proc.c). The build is the project's Makefile (the static library and the test programs); the test runs the table tests and the Unicode 18.0.0 normalization and grapheme-break conformance files, which support/utf8proc/fetch-test-data.sh downloads once into $CACHE and checks against their SHA-256.
build: make -j"$JOBS" CC="$CC" libutf8proc.a test/normtest test/graphemetest test/case test/custom test/charwidth test/misc test/maxdecomposition test/valid test/iterate
test: for t in charwidth misc valid iterate case custom maxdecomposition; do test/$t || exit 1; done

configs.name: zstd
configs.notes: Zstandard: compression contexts and workspaces carved out of one allocation (ZSTD_cwksp), entropy tables and match finders over caller buffers, a dictionary builder (divsufsort, COVER), multithreaded compression through a thread pool. The build is the library and the CLI (lib-release, zstd-release) and tests/Makefile's datagen, fuzzer and zstreamtest; the test is playTests.sh without its long tests (what tests/Makefile's check runs, run directly because check rebuilds programs/zstd with debug flags), 300 fuzzer and 100 zstreamtest tests with seed 1 (the seed is fixed: left alone both take it from the time), and a dictionary round trip: zstd --train over lib/, then every source of lib/compress and lib/decompress compressed at -13 with the dictionary, decompressed and compared.
build: make -j"$JOBS" -C tests CC="$CC" datagen fuzzer zstreamtest
test: mkdir -p gate-dict && programs/zstd -q --train -r lib -o gate-dict/dict && for f in lib/compress/*.c lib/decompress/*.c; do b=gate-dict/$(basename "$f"); programs/zstd -q -f -13 -D gate-dict/dict "$f" -o "$b.zst" && programs/zstd -q -f -d -D gate-dict/dict "$b.zst" -o "$b" && cmp "$f" "$b" || exit 1; done

configs.name: libuv
configs.notes: An event loop: handles and requests embedded in caller-owned structures, linked into the loop's intrusive queues (uv__queue) and found again through container_of, close callbacks that run after uv_close returns, a thread pool, kqueue and FSEvents on Darwin. The build is the project's CMake build of the static test runner (uv_run_tests_a, which needs BUILD_TESTING with the shared library enabled); the test is support/libuv/run-tests.sh, which runs every test in its own process from the source directory except four that fail on Darwin with the reference compiler too: emfile (fails every run: uv_tcp_connect returns UV_EMFILE at test-emfile.c:93), spawn_exercise_sigchld_issue (exercises the kernel's lost SIGCHLD; timed out in both of two reference runs of the suite and passes alone) and udp_multicast_join and udp_multicast_join6 (need multicast on the host's interfaces; timed out in one of the two).

configs.name: oniguruma
configs.notes: A backtracking regular-expression library: a parser building node trees, a compiler to bytecode in growable buffers, a matcher with an explicit backtrack stack (alloca, then the heap), per-encoding tables reached through function pointers in OnigEncodingType. The build is the project's CMake build, static, with the POSIX API and its test programs; the test runs them (test_utf8, test_syntax, test_options, testc (EUC-JP), testcu (UTF-16), testp (POSIX API), test_regset, test_back), each of which exits non-zero on any failed or erroneous case. The per-file compiles use support/oniguruma/config.h, which CMake generates.
test: for t in test_utf8 test_syntax test_options testc testcu testp test_regset test_back; do out/test/$t || exit 1; done

configs.name: redis
configs.notes: An in-memory data-structure server: sds strings with headers before the returned pointer, listpacks and quicklists packed into byte arrays, incrementally rehashed dicts, rax radix trees, an event loop with callbacks, reference-counted robj values. The build is the project's Makefile without jemalloc (MALLOC=libc) and TLS, with CLANG=clang because src/Makefile tells clang from `$(CC) --version` (the gate's compiler wrapper prints weavec-cc's version) and OPTIMIZATION=-O2 because its default -O3 adds -flto; the test is support/redis/run-tests.sh: the Tcl suite's list, hash, set, zset, string, incr, expire, keyspace, sort, scan and hyperloglog units with 4 clients (it links tests/tmp to a directory under /tmp: the test servers' Unix socket paths must stay under Darwin's 104 bytes). The per-file compiles are the core data-structure and command sources; release.c needs the release.h the build generates and server.c is left out for its size.
build: make -j"$JOBS" CC="$CC" MALLOC=libc BUILD_TLS=no CLANG=clang OPTIMIZATION=-O2
test: sh "$SUPPORT/run-tests.sh" unit/type/list unit/type/hash unit/type/set unit/type/zset unit/type/string unit/type/incr unit/expire unit/keyspace unit/sort unit/scan unit/hyperloglog

lowered.note: the latent null dereference triaged true at src/cluster_legacy.c:237-238 (auxHumanNodenameSetter's `!n` branch)

configs.name: expat
configs.notes: A stream-oriented XML parser: tokenizers instantiated per encoding from xmltok_impl.c, a parser object with handler function pointers and growable pools of strings (STRING_POOL), hash tables of entities and attributes, its own allocator hooks (XML_Memory_Handling_Suite) and billion-laughs accounting. The CMake project is in expat/; the build is its static library, xmlwf, three examples and the C test runner (runtests_cxx is C++ and not built); the test is runtests (4,512 checks), xmlwf over testdata/largefiles (nine documents of 3 to 36 MB) and doc/xmlwf.xml, and the examples over nes96.xml and xmlwf.xml. The per-file compiles use support/expat/expat_config.h, which CMake generates.
build: cmake --build out -j "$JOBS" --target runtests xmlwf elements outline element_declarations
test: for f in testdata/largefiles/*.xml testdata/largefiles/*.rdf expat/doc/xmlwf.xml; do out/xmlwf/xmlwf -n -t "$f" || exit 1; done

out/examples/outline < testdata/largefiles/nes96.xml > /dev/null && out/examples/elements < testdata/largefiles/nes96.xml > /dev/null && out/examples/element_declarations < expat/doc/xmlwf.xml > /dev/null

configs.name: pcre2
configs.notes: Perl-compatible regular expressions: a compiler to a code-unit-width-generic bytecode (each source built for 8-, 16- and 32-bit units), an interpreter with a heap-allocated backtracking frame vector, a DFA matcher, match data and contexts with allocator hooks. The build is the project's CMake build of the three libraries, pcre2test, pcre2grep and the POSIX test, without JIT (its default; the JIT needs the deps/sljit submodule, which the gate's checkout leaves empty, and generates machine code no compiler sees), readline, libz or libbz2; the test is CTest: RunTest over all three widths, RunGrepTest and pcre2posix_test. The per-file compiles (8-bit) use support/pcre2/config.h and pcre2.h, which CMake generates.

configs.name: libevent
configs.notes: An event-notification library: event structures owned by callers and linked into a base's maps and heaps (evmap, min_heap), backends selected through a function-pointer table (eventop), evbuffers of chained, reference-counted segments, bufferevents with deferred callbacks, an HTTP server and client and an asynchronous DNS resolver. The build is the project's CMake build, static, without OpenSSL, Mbed TLS and the benchmarks (the regress suite is generated with python3); the test is CTest without the regress entries (the small test programs over the select, poll and kqueue backends and the rate-limit tests), then regress (over 300 tests, about 80 s of timers each) twice, once on kqueue and once on poll in debug mode, instead of CTest's six runs, which take twice as long. Both leave out dns/initialize_nameservers, which fails with any compiler on a host whose first nameserver is IPv6 (regress_dns.c:1021 expects sizeof(struct sockaddr), gets 28). The tests run one at a time: under ctest -j 8 the fdleak tests and the ratelim tests failed with either compiler, up to six a run with the reference compiler. test-ratelim__group_lim is left out: it failed in two of three serial runs of the reference compiler's build (a timing tolerance).

configs.name: libsodium
configs.notes: A cryptography library: constant-time arithmetic over fixed-size limb arrays (ed25519 ref10, curve25519), stream ciphers and MACs over caller buffers, Argon2 over a large heap region of blocks, guarded allocations (sodium_malloc: guard pages around a canary, mprotect), implementations chosen at run time through function pointers (sodium_runtime_*). The pinned commit ships its generated configure and Makefile.in, so no autotools are needed: the build is ./configure (static) and make, then make check TESTS= to build the 80 test programs of test/default; the test is make check, which runs them and compares each one's output with its .exp file. The per-file compiles are the portable implementations (no SSE, AVX or ARM-crypto variants) with the definitions configure finds on darwin-arm64, and use support/libsodium/sodium/version.h, which configure generates.

configs.name: libxml2
configs.notes: SEALED (RFC 0033, section 11): built with the reference compiler only until gate D2. An XML toolkit: a DOM of doubly linked nodes freed recursively, a string dictionary with reference counts, push and pull parsers, XPath, schemas and HTML, with allocator hooks (xmlMalloc). The build is the project's CMake build, static, without Python, iconv, ICU, lzma, zlib, HTTP or readline; the test is CTest (runtest, runsuite, testapi, testchar, testdict, testparser, testrecurse; runxmlconf needs the W3C suite, which is not in the repository, and is not added). The per-file compiles use support/libxml2/config.h and libxml/xmlversion.h, which CMake generates.

configs.name: libpng
configs.notes: SEALED (RFC 0033, section 11): built with the reference compiler only until gate D2. The PNG reference library: row buffers and transformations over caller memory, chunk parsing, longjmp-based error handling (png_error), progressive reading through callbacks, NEON filter functions on arm64; zlib is the SDK's. The build is the project's CMake build with the tests and tools (its tests link the shared library, which they require); the test is CTest (pngtest, the pngvalid, pngstest and pngunknown runs, 33 tests). The per-file compiles use support/libpng/pnglibconf.h, which CMake generates.

configs.name: mbedtls

lowered.note: metatest's deliberate read after free (framework/tests/programs/metatest.c:158), triaged true
metatest's deliberate double free (framework/tests/programs/metatest.c:168), triaged true

configs.notes: SEALED (RFC 0033, section 11): built with the reference compiler only until gate D2. A TLS and cryptography library: multi-precision integers in limb arrays, cipher and message-digest contexts dispatched through info tables, the PSA key store, X.509 and ASN.1 parsers over caller buffers, the TLS record layer. Its CMake build needs the framework submodule, which the gate's checkout leaves empty: support/mbedtls/fetch-framework.sh fetches it once into $CACHE at the commit the pinned commit records and copies it in (the generated library sources are committed; the test suites are generated with python3's standard library). The build is the library, the programs and the test suites (MBEDTLS_FATAL_WARNINGS off: the project builds with -Werror and a new compiler's warnings are not its bugs); the test is CTest, serially (135 suites in about 20 s: the PSA storage and ITS suites keep their files in the shared working directory and fail when run in parallel), and programs/test/selftest.

configs.name: msgpack-c
configs.notes: SEALED (RFC 0033, section 11): built with the reference compiler only until gate D2. MessagePack for C: objects allocated from chunked zones (msgpack_zone) and freed with them, an unpacker with a growable, reference-counted buffer, packers writing through a callback, vrefbuffer chains of iovecs. Its test suite is C++ on GoogleTest, which this machine does not have, so the test is the examples: simple_c, lib_buffer_unpack and user_buffer_unpack, whose output must equal the reference build's (support/msgpack-c/*.out), boundary (asserts its round trips) and the two speed tests. The build is the project's CMake build, static (BUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF links the examples statically). The per-file compiles use support/msgpack-c/msgpack/sysdep.h and pack_template.h, which CMake generates.
test: for e in simple_c lib_buffer_unpack user_buffer_unpack; do out/example/$e > out/$e.out && cmp out/$e.out "$SUPPORT/$e.out" || exit 1; done

configs.name: yyjson
configs.notes: SEALED (RFC 0033, section 11): built with the reference compiler only until gate D2. A JSON library: immutable documents as flat arrays of values with lengths packed into tags, mutable documents of circular linked lists in pooled memory, hand-written number parsing and printing, unaligned loads and stores over caller buffers, allocator hooks. The build is the project's CMake build with its tests (two of which compile yyjson.h as C++); the test is CTest (12 tests over test/data).

configs.name: quickjs
configs.notes: A JavaScript engine: reference-counted JSValues (tagged structs) over objects with shapes and property arrays, a cycle-collecting GC over intrusive list.h lists (container_of), atoms, strings and ropes, a bytecode compiler and interpreter with its own value stack, a regexp engine and Unicode tables (libregexp, libunicode), dtoa, allocation through JSMallocFunctions, and quickjs-libc's std/os modules with workers (threads). The build is the project's Makefile (-O2) with explicit targets: qjs, qjsc, run-test262, libquickjs.a and the three examples (hello, test_fib, hello_module, which qjsc compiles with $CC). quickjs.check.o (the Makefile's CONFIG_CHECK_JSVALUE build, compile-only by the project's own account; JS_GetOpaque always returns null in it) is left out of the build: WeaveC's definite null dereferences there are true but vacuous (RFC 0034, gate F1), and lowering them would need one triage entry per finding and would lower null-dereference errors across the whole build. The default target `all` builds it (and qjs.check.o), so the build names the targets; `make test` depends only on qjs on Darwin (the bjson and point shared-library tests are off there), so it builds no check object. The test is `make test` (tests/test_*.js: closures, language, builtins, loops, BigInt, cyclic imports, a worker, std/os, rw handlers) and the three examples against their expected output; run-test262 is built but not run (test262 is a separate checkout of the conformance suite). The per-file compiles are the six library sources with the Makefile's defines (-D_GNU_SOURCE, CONFIG_VERSION from VERSION) and its -funsigned-char -fwrapv.
build: make -j"$JOBS" CC="$CC" qjs qjsc run-test262 libquickjs.a examples/hello examples/test_fib examples/hello_module

configs.name: lmdb
configs.notes: The Lightning memory-mapped database (libraries/liblmdb): a copy-on-write B+tree whose pages are read through pointers into a memory-mapped file (page headers, node offsets and overflow pages by pointer arithmetic), dirty pages in malloc'd buffers, free-page ID lists (midl), cursors with page stacks, a reader table in a shared lock file, nested transactions, and a crypto/checksum module hook (module.c). The build is liblmdb's Makefile (-O2 -g -pthread): the static and shared library and the five tools, with VERSION_OPT=-Wl,-current_version,1.0 (the Makefile's Mac OS X value; its default -soname is a GNU ld option), then mtest..mtest5 with support/lmdb/fixed-seed.h forced in (mtest, mtest2, mtest3 and mtest5 seed rand() with time(NULL); the header fixes the seed so the tests are deterministic). The test is support/lmdb/run-tests.sh: each mtest against a fresh testdb (what `make test` does for mtest), and over mtest's database mdb_stat, an mdb_dump / mdb_load round trip and mdb_copy (plain and compacting), compared record by record. mtest6, mtest_remap and mtest_enc* are not built: none is among the Makefile's default programs (its rall target, for MDB_VL32 / MDB_RPAGE_CACHE builds, adds the remap and two encryption tests). The per-file compiles are the library (mdb.c, midl.c, module.c) and the five tools.
build: cd libraries/liblmdb && make -j"$JOBS" CC="$CC" VERSION_OPT=-Wl,-current_version,1.0 liblmdb.a liblmdb.so.1.0 mdb_stat mdb_copy mdb_dump mdb_load mdb_drop
cd libraries/liblmdb && make -j"$JOBS" CC="$CC" XCFLAGS="-include $SUPPORT/fixed-seed.h" mtest mtest2 mtest3 mtest4 mtest5

bench.name: lmdb-put-get
build: cd libraries/liblmdb && "$CC" -O2 -pthread -I. -c "$BENCH/lmdb-bench.c" -o lmdb-bench.o && "$CC" -pthread -o lmdb-bench lmdb-bench.o liblmdb.a
bench.command: rm -rf bench-db && libraries/liblmdb/lmdb-bench bench-db > bench.out && cat bench.out

configs.name: janet
configs.notes: A Lisp-like language and its bytecode VM: NaN-boxed values, a mark-and-sweep GC with a header in front of every object (janet_gcalloc), fibers with their own growable stacks, buffers, arrays, tables and interned strings and structs, abstract types with vtables, setjmp/longjmp panics, a PEG engine, marshalling, an event loop with threads and sockets, and an FFI. The build is the project's Makefile (`make`, CFLAGS default -O2 -g), which bootstraps: it compiles src/core/*.c and src/boot/*.c with -DJANET_BOOTSTRAP -O0 into build/janet_boot, runs janet_boot to generate the amalgamated build/c/janet.c (the core sources plus the compiled boot image), compiles that with -O2 into build/janet, libjanet.a and libjanet.dylib, and runs build/janet to write build/janet.h; so the build runs code the compiler built. The test is `make test`: every test/suite*.janet (stopping at the first failure) and every example compiled with -k; suite-ev opens sockets on localhost port 8761 (JANET_TEST_PORT). The per-file compiles are the 40 core sources and the shell (src/mainclient/shell.c) without -DJANET_BOOTSTRAP, as the amalgamated janet.c compiles them.

configs.name: brotli
configs.notes: Brotli: encoder state and ring buffer, hashers and block splitters carved out of BrotliAllocate'd arenas through allocator hooks (memory.c), Huffman tables and a decoder state machine over caller buffers, the static dictionary and transforms. The build is the project's CMake build, static (BUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF), with the CLI; the test is its CTest suite (73 round-trip and compatibility tests over tests/testdata), then round trips with the CLI of seven test files (text, binary, random, empty, one byte, a source file) at qualities 0-11 and windows 10/16/24, a large-window (--large_window=26) round trip of bb.binast, and a raw-dictionary (-D) round trip. Bench: the CLI compressing the 64 MiB zlib-input.py text at -q 7 and decompressing it.
test: mkdir -p gate-rt && for f in tests/testdata/alice29.txt tests/testdata/mapsdatazrh tests/testdata/random_org_10k.bin tests/testdata/zerosukkanooa tests/testdata/empty tests/testdata/x c/enc/encode.c; do for q in 0 1 2 3 5 7 9 10 11; do for w in 10 16 24; do out/brotli -q $q --lgwin=$w -c "$f" > gate-rt/c.br && out/brotli -d -c gate-rt/c.br > gate-rt/d && cmp gate-rt/d "$f" || { echo "FAIL q$q w$w $f"; exit 1; }; done; done; done

mkdir -p gate-rt && out/brotli -q 9 --large_window=26 -c tests/testdata/bb.binast > gate-rt/l.br && out/brotli -d --large_window=26 -c gate-rt/l.br | cmp - tests/testdata/bb.binast && out/brotli -q 6 -D tests/testdata/alice29.txt -c tests/testdata/asyoulik.txt > gate-rt/dict.br && out/brotli -d -D tests/testdata/alice29.txt -c gate-rt/dict.br | cmp - tests/testdata/asyoulik.txt && out/brotli -t --large_window=26 gate-rt/l.br

configs.name: xz
configs.notes: XZ Utils' liblzma: coder chains of lzma_next_coder structs allocated through lzma_allocator hooks and freed through end callbacks, the LZ match finders' hash chains and binary trees over a sliding window, the range coder, BCJ and delta filters in place over caller buffers, the multithreaded encoder and decoder (worker threads, an output queue), index trees. The build is the project's CMake build (liblzma static, the xz, xzdec, lzmadec and lzmainfo tools, the tests) with XZ_NLS=OFF (no gettext, so nothing links Homebrew's libintl); the test is its CTest suite (22 tests: the liblzma unit tests, test_compress on generated files, test_files.sh over tests/files, test_scripts.sh, test_suffix.sh), then round trips with the CLI of liblzma's concatenated sources, an empty file and doc/faq.txt at presets -0 to -9e, multithreaded with small blocks, through the x86, arm64 and delta filters, in the .lzma format, through xzdec and lzmadec, raw LZMA1, plus xz -t and xz -l -vv. Bench: xz -6 -T1 compressing the 8 MiB zlib-input.py text and decompressing it. The per-file compiles use support/xz/config.h, the definitions CMake passes to liblzma written as a header (sysdefs.h includes it under HAVE_CONFIG_H); 45 of liblzma's 77 sources: the check, LZ, LZMA, range-coder and delta sources, the simple-filter core with x86 and arm64, and the block, index, stream (single and multithreaded), filter, alone, lzip and string-conversion sources of common/.
test: mkdir -p gate-rt && cat src/liblzma/*/*.c > gate-rt/src && : > gate-rt/empty && X=out/xz && for f in gate-rt/src gate-rt/empty doc/faq.txt; do for o in -0 -1 -3 -6 -9e "-6 -T4 --block-size=64KiB" "--x86 --lzma2=preset=6" "--arm64 --lzma2" "--delta=dist=4 --lzma2=preset=1 --check=sha256" "--format=lzma"; do $X $o -c "$f" > gate-rt/c && $X -d -c gate-rt/c | cmp - "$f" || { echo "FAIL $o $f"; exit 1; }; done; $X -c "$f" > gate-rt/c.xz && out/xzdec gate-rt/c.xz | cmp - "$f" && $X -t gate-rt/c.xz && $X -l -vv gate-rt/c.xz > /dev/null && $X --format=lzma -c "$f" | out/lzmadec | cmp - "$f" && $X --format=raw --lzma1=preset=2 -c "$f" | $X --format=raw --lzma1 -d -c | cmp - "$f" || { echo "FAIL tools $f"; exit 1; }; done

configs.name: libdeflate
configs.notes: libdeflate: whole-buffer DEFLATE, zlib and gzip compression and decompression; compressors with hash-chain, binary-tree and hash-table match finders in one large allocation (custom allocator hooks, libdeflate_set_memory_allocator), decompression tables in the decompressor struct, word-at-a-time copies near buffer ends, Adler-32 and CRC-32 with arm64 NEON/PMULL paths chosen at run time. The build is the project's CMake build with LIBDEFLATE_BUILD_TESTS=ON (static and shared libraries; the programs link the static one; the tests use the SDK's zlib for comparisons); the test is CTest (8 test programs), then scripts/exec_tests.sh (each test program again and the benchmark program in deflate, gzip and zlib formats, at levels 0-12, checked against zlib with -Y/-Z) and scripts/gzip_tests.sh (libdeflate-gzip against itself, as scripts/run_tests.sh --quick does) over a 1,000,000-byte TESTDATA made from the project's sources in sorted order (run_tests.sh uses find's unsorted order). Bench: libdeflate-gzip compressing the 64 MiB zlib-input.py text at -1, -6 and -9 and decompressing each. The per-file compiles are the library's sources and the arm64 cpu_features.c (x86/cpu_features.c compiles to nothing on arm64).
test: cat lib/*.c lib/*.h lib/*/*.h programs/*.c programs/*.h scripts/*.sh | head -c 1000000 > gate-testdata && WRAPPER= TESTDATA="$PWD/gate-testdata" sh ./scripts/exec_tests.sh out/programs > /dev/null

cat lib/*.c lib/*.h lib/*/*.h programs/*.c programs/*.h scripts/*.sh | head -c 1000000 > gate-testdata && GZIP="$PWD/out/programs/libdeflate-gzip" GUNZIP="$PWD/out/programs/libdeflate-gzip -d" TESTDATA="$PWD/gate-testdata" bash ./scripts/gzip_tests.sh

bench.name: libdeflate-gzip
bench.command: for l in 1 6 9; do ./out/programs/libdeflate-gzip -$l -c "$INPUT" > bench.gz && ./out/programs/libdeflate-gzip -d -c bench.gz > /dev/null || exit 1; done

configs.name: zlib-ng
configs.notes: zlib-ng, built zlib-compatible (ZLIB_COMPAT=ON): the deflate and inflate state, window and pending buffer allocated in one aligned block through zalloc/zfree hooks, deflate strategies (quick, fast, medium, slow, rle, huff, stored) over the window, chunked copies and a function table of arm64 NEON/CRC/PMULL implementations chosen at run time, gz* file wrappers. The build is the project's CMake build with ZLIB_COMPAT=ON and WITH_GTEST=OFF: its GoogleTest suite is C++ and fetches googletest from the network, so it is off (WITH_FUZZERS also stays off, since it enables C++ in the project); the test is CTest's C tests (69: example, infcover, the CVE and GitHub-issue regressions, minigzip and minideflate over test/data at every level and strategy, makefixed/maketrees/makecrct), then support/zlib-ng/round-trips.sh: minigzip round trips of the library's concatenated sources, an empty file and test/data's JPEG and text at levels 0-9 and strategies -h/-R/-F/-f/-T, and minideflate round trips at levels 1/6/9 and windows 9/12/15. Bench: minigzip compressing the 64 MiB zlib-input.py text at -1, -6 and -9 and decompressing each. The per-file compiles are the 38 sources of the arm64 build (generic and arm, with CMake's definitions; the NEON, dotprod and PMULL files compile without their -march flags) and use the headers CMake generates, copied into support/zlib-ng/.

bench.name: zlib-ng-minigzip
bench.command: for l in 1 6 9; do ./out/minigzip -$l < "$INPUT" > bench.gz && ./out/minigzip -d < bench.gz > /dev/null || exit 1; done

configs.name: curl
configs.notes: libcurl and the curl tool: transfer and connection state machines over intrusive linked lists, hash tables, splay trees and uint tables, dynbuf and bufq buffers, connection filters chained through function pointers, a multi handle owning easy handles, its own printf (mprintf), the URL API and the cookie, header, chunked and FTP-listing parsers. The build is the project's CMake build with the milestone evaluation's options (no TLS, IDN, PSL, SSH, zstd, brotli, nghttp2 or LDAP; zlib is the SDK's): the library, the tool, the examples and the test programs (target testdeps: libtests, units, tunits, the test servers). The test is runtests.pl run from out/tests over a fixed selection: tests 1-999 (HTTP, FTP, file://, cookies, proxies, globbing, the libtests 500-699), 1300-1399 (unit tests, more HTTP and FTP) and 1500-1699 (multi-interface libtests, the URL API test 1560, unit tests 1600-1699): 1015 tests at the reference, about 70 s with 4 jobs on an idle machine. Tests keyworded flaky or timing-dependent are disabled ('!', not the milestone's '~', so none runs with its result ignored); -a goes on after a failure and the exit status is then 1; --min=1000 fails the run when test servers do not start, since runtests.pl only skips a test whose server fails. The tests needing a Unix-socket server (1435, 1436, 1467, 1468, 1470) are outside the selection: under the gate's directory their socket paths exceed Darwin's 104 bytes, and they would be skipped after a 30 s wait each. A few selected tests skip for features this build lacks (SSL, crypto, NTLM, PSL, debug) or because 'ip6-localhost' does not resolve. The bench (test/corpus/bench/curl-bench.c) links the static libcurl, built alone, and for 10 rounds parses 20,000 generated URLs with the URL API (every part read back, a relative reference resolved, a query appended), escapes, unescapes and parses a date for each, and loads 5,000 cookie lines through CURLOPT_COOKIELIST, read back with CURLINFO_COOKIELIST: libcurl's own parsing, allocation and list code with no transfer, so no socket or kernel time (file:// transfers spend most of their time in the kernel, --trace in libc's stdio); it prints one checksum line. The per-file compiles are 45 library sources with support/curl/curl_config.h, which CMake generates.
test: cd out/tests && perl ../../tests/runtests.pl -a -p -j"$JOBS" --min=1000 '!flaky' '!timing-dependent' 1 to 999 1300 to 1399 1500 to 1699

configs.name: cmark
configs.notes: The CommonMark reference implementation: a tree of malloc'd nodes linked by parent, child and sibling pointers and freed iteratively, allocation through a cmark_mem table of function pointers, growable cmark_strbuf buffers, chunks pointing into the input, a re2c scanner, the inline parser's delimiter stack and bracket list, a reference map, an iterator and five renderers. The build is the project's CMake Release build (static library, the cmark executable and api_test, which has one C++ file built by CMake's default C++ compiler); the test is CTest: api_test, html_normalization and the spec, smart-punctuation and regression tests through the executable (5 tests; the spec tests need python3). The library tests (spectest_library, pathological, roundtrip, entity) exist only with BUILD_SHARED_LIBS, which is off by default on this platform, as in the milestone evaluation. The bench concatenates test/spec.txt 160 times (33 MB, in bench.build, from the pinned checkout) and renders it with --smart to HTML, XML, LaTeX, man and CommonMark into /dev/null (no output); its check compares the SHA-256 of the five renderings with a pinned value. The per-file compiles are the 20 src/*.c with support/cmark/cmark_export.h and cmark_version.h, which CMake generates, in C23 as CMake 3.21 and later build them.

bench.name: cmark-spec-render
build: i=0; while [ $i -lt 160 ]; do cat test/spec.txt; i=$((i+1)); done > bench.md
bench.command: for t in html xml latex man commonmark; do bench-out/src/cmark --smart -t $t bench.md > /dev/null || exit 1; done
bench.check: test "$(for t in html xml latex man commonmark; do bench-out/src/cmark --smart -t $t bench.md; done | shasum -a 256 | cut -c1-64)" = 9e0efde0132b65579bea7e2a0d4a3fae8f2f99dced288443eff65e866232e7c1

configs.name: libgit2
configs.notes: The Git library: reference-counted objects in a cache, an object database with loose and pack backends reading packs through mmap'd windows, delta application, the index, tree and diff iterators, the refdb, diff and merge over xdiff, a utility layer of git_str buffers, vectors, pools and hash maps, allocation through a table of function pointers (git__malloc). Bundled code in this build: SHA-1 with collision detection, SHA-256, llhttp and xdiff; zlib is the system's (the SDK's) and regular expressions use the system's regcomp_l (the zlib and PCRE under deps/ are not built). The build is the project's CMake build with the milestone evaluation's options (no HTTPS, SSH, GSSAPI or NTLM; tests on): the library, the git2 CLI and the two clar runners. The test is util_tests (the utility layer, every test) and libgit2_tests over 38 suites selected with -s: core, date, delta, message, patch, path, object, odb, refs, index, diff, status, config, revwalk, pack, merge, apply, blame, commit, describe, email, filter, graph, ignore, iterator, mailmap, notes, rebase, reset, revert, cherrypick, stash, attr, repo, grafts, fetchhead, remote and threads (about 2,500 tests, 70-90 s at the reference, most of it in the kernel copying fixtures); clar exits non-zero on any failure. Left out: online (the network); checkout, whose checkout::icase::overwrites_links_for_folders_when_forced fails with the reference compiler too (macOS's case-insensitive file system); clone (76 s, mostly waiting), network, submodule and worktree (slow and file-system bound); stress and perf (60 s and 5 s of load tests); and the empty or Windows-only win32, trace, stream, transport and transports. The bench (test/corpus/bench/libgit2-bench.c) links the static library, built without tests or CLI, and builds a 1,500-commit history in memory (a mempack-only object database and an empty configuration, so no file system and no user configuration): each commit edits two of eight generated files, writes blobs, a tree and a commit, renders each edit's patch (git_patch_from_buffers) and merges it three-way with an unrelated edit (git_merge_file); then a revision walk diffs every commit against its parent with stats. Its time is mostly xdiff and SHA-1; it prints one checksum line. The per-file compiles are 45 sources of src/util, src/libgit2, deps/xdiff and deps/llhttp with support/libgit2/git2_features.h and experimental.h, which CMake generates, in C90 as the build compiles them.

configs.name: libjpeg-turbo
configs.notes: SEALED (RFC 0034, section 9): built with the reference compiler only until gate F2. The JPEG codec behind libjpeg and the TurboJPEG API: a pool allocator (jmemmgr) handing out small objects and 2-D sample arrays (row pointer tables over one large block), method tables of function pointers in every module, virtual sample arrays, 8/12/16-bit sample code compiled three times from the same sources through src/wrapper/*-N.c, Huffman bit buffers over caller buffers, longjmp error recovery in TurboJPEG, NEON SIMD on arm64. The build is the project's CMake build in Release with its defaults: static and shared libraries (the tests run both), TurboJPEG, the tools and the tests, and the SIMD extensions on (on arm64 they are NEON intrinsics and GAS assembly, which the compiler builds without nasm). The test is CTest (664 tests: the cjpeg/djpeg/jpegtran MD5 comparisons over testimages/, tjunittest, the examples). The per-file compiles use the three headers CMake generates (jconfig.h, jconfigint.h, jversion.h) from support/libjpeg-turbo; they cover the format-independent sources and the 8-bit wrappers of the rest.

configs.name: opus
configs.notes: SEALED (RFC 0034, section 9): built with the reference compiler only until gate F2. The Opus audio codec (SILK + CELT): encoder and decoder states laid out as one allocation with the sub-codec states at computed offsets (opus_decoder_get_size, align()), variable-length stack arrays (VAR_ARRAYS) and a range coder over caller buffers, multistream and projection wrappers carving several codec states out of one block, packet parsing and repacketizing with extension padding, float and fixed-point DSP with NEON intrinsics on arm64. The build is the project's CMake build in Release with OPUS_BUILD_TESTING (static library, the five test programs); the deep-learning features (DRED, OSCE, which need downloaded model weights) are off, as they are by default, and so are the programs, which no test uses. The test is CTest (test_opus_api, _decode, _encode, _padding, _extensions) with SEED=1: left alone the decode, encode and extensions tests take their random seed from the time. The per-file compiles use the definitions of the CMake build and its config.h (support/opus, only PACKAGE_VERSION).

configs.name: flac
configs.notes: SEALED (RFC 0034, section 9): built with the reference compiler only until gate F2. The Free Lossless Audio Codec: a bit reader and writer over growable word buffers, encoder and decoder objects with private structs behind opaque handles and per-channel buffers allocated with padding for the LPC and residual code, metadata blocks as owned trees (Vorbis comments, cue sheets, pictures, seek tables) copied, resized and freed by metadata_object.c, a metadata chain editor over files, multithreaded encoding, NEON LPC on arm64. The build is the project's CMake build in Release without Ogg, the C++ libraries, the docs and the man pages, with the tests, the programs (flac, metaflac) and the examples. The first step pins the random seeds of the two test programs that seed random() from gettimeofday (test_streams, which generates the noise streams, and test_seeking, which picks random seek targets) to 1, in the copy only, so that every run sees the same data. The test is CTest without its streams test (libFLAC, grabbag, generate_streams, flac, metaflac, replaygain, seeking, compression), then the streams script run directly at FLAC__TEST_LEVEL=0 (about 1200 encode, decode and compare round trips): CTest sets level 1, at which it alone takes 300 s with the reference compiler. The per-file compiles use the CMake build's config.h (support/flac).
build: perl -pi -e 's/srandom\(tv\.tv_usec\)/srandom(1)/' src/test_streams/main.c src/test_seeking/main.c && grep -q 'srandom(1)' src/test_streams/main.c && grep -q 'srandom(1)' src/test_seeking/main.c

configs.name: giflib
configs.notes: SEALED (RFC 0034, section 9): built with the reference compiler only until gate F2. GIFLIB, the GIF reader and writer: decoder and encoder state behind a GifFileType handle with a private struct, an LZW decoder and encoder with a hash table and a prefix stack, saved images as arrays of structs with owned color maps, extension blocks and raster buffers grown with reallocarray, I/O through read and write callbacks, color quantization; the utilities copy, filter, dump and build GIFs. The checkout is the canonical SourceForge repository. The build is the top-level Makefile's static library and its 14 utilities: its default target also builds libutil.dylib, which does not link on Darwin (qprintf.o needs GifErrorString from libgif) with the reference compiler, and nothing uses the shared libraries. The test is support/giflib/run-tests.sh: tests/makefile's regression targets (51 TAP checks of the utilities against recorded dumps, colormaps and RGB files) through tapview, as `make check` does, with giffix-regress run by the script itself with a portable `head -c`, because the makefile uses GNU head's `--bytes=-20`, which BSD head rejects. The per-file compiles cover every C file of the top directory (library, getarg/qprintf and the utilities).
build: make -j"$JOBS" CC="$CC" static-lib gifbuild giffix giftext giftool gifclrmp gifbg gifcolor gifecho giffilter gifhisto gifinto gifsponge gifwedge gif2rgb

configs.name: wren
configs.notes: SEALED (RFC 0034, section 9): built with the reference compiler only until gate F2. Wren, a small class-based scripting language: a single-pass compiler emitting bytecode into growable buffers, a stack VM over NaN-tagged values (doubles and object pointers packed in 64 bits), fibers with their own growable stacks and call frames (pointers into the stack rebased when it moves), a mark-and-sweep collector over an intrusive object list with a gray stack, strings, lists, maps (open addressing) and ranges as flexible objects, foreign objects with user data, and the embedding API's slots and handles. The build is projects/make.mac's release_64bit configuration (libwren.a and .dylib, bin/wren_test); the test is util/test.py, which runs bin/wren_test over test/ (866 scripts with their expected output, errors and exit codes, the API tests in C included) and exits non-zero on any failure. The per-file compiles cover the VM, the optional modules and the test host.
